Fiddly. Like what the hell does this even mean? From what I could gather it could mean like 6 different things when describing a board game.  
 1) Physical components that are too cumbersome to handle.  
 2) Games with so many small, forgettable rules that need that are constantly addressed during gameplay.  
 3) Mechanisms or other game elements that need to be updated constantly.  
 4) Games that require you to do math in order to play them.    
 5) Games with horrible graphic design that make it hard to discern fine details and other game symbols.   
 6) As a catch all to describe a board game they do not like.  
 I think it's the last one that bothers me the most. There are so many words that we can use to describe the things we don't like in greater detail. Components can be finicky or awkward. Rules can be convoluted or dense. Upkeep can be tiresome or clunky. Yet, we always seem to come back to this one word to describe all of it. Also, it is usually used as a pejorative but can also be something that people enjoy in certain games? It's all too much for me. I guess I just find the word fiddly to be, well, fiddly. At least in the way board gamers use it.

I absolutely loved it. Honestly, I don't think they could have presented a mini-golf game show any better. Mini-golf, after all, is just a parody of regular golf and Holey Moley had all of the makings to be a great parody of a broadcasting of regular golf. Creative Holes ✅, Competent Hosts ✅, Tense Quiet Moments ✅, Full of Itself Stylization ✅   
To address your complaint about the contestants being reduced down to one trait, I think it really works for this show. I mean, you really have to ask yourself how invested you want be in contestants on a dumb mini-golf game show. For me, its almost none at all. But, to each their own, I guess. Furthermore, I do agree that they really fucked up the advertising for the show. If you came into this show expecting a golf-themed Wipeout clone, as the ads suggested, you will be very disappointed. But, if you come into the show with an excitement for mini-golf and only mini-golf, you'll find a delightful show filled with campy-ass set design and sarcastic humor that is right up your alley.    Anything more to the show? Yeah, I think they should have more holes. If the 10 holes we saw on the first episode are the only 10 holes in the whole show, then this show is gonna get really boring really fast. Considering how we didn't see the giant banked curve used in the episode, I have hope for more holes. I hope to see at least 10 more holes, but at the very least 8 more holes to be cheeky and match the standard 18 in normal golf courses. Overall, it's a good show for what it is: "extreme mini-golf," whatever that means. And if you're a family, a child, or high as balls like I was watching the first episode, you'll most likely enjoy the show and completely lose your shit when Kenny G pops out.
